title: Frozen Polatory Python workflow and logical array surface
purpose: Provide a machine-readable inventory of the Python workflows, logical array shapes, inputs, outputs, and stable error-category domains that must be represented by the RapidRBF Python migration.

decision_basis.accepted_requirement: Python workflow and array-shape coverage under the rapidrbf package migration

contract.target_api_design_rule: A documented and mechanically checkable RapidRBF path must cover each accepted workflow and logical shape; it need not reproduce the frozen import names or call signatures.

evidence_limits.array_semantics_basis: C++ binding types and accepted compatibility resolution

symbols.n: input point or value row count
symbols.g: gradient-constraint or gradient-evaluation point row count

dtype_vocabulary.signed_integer: signed integer values with target storage width not fixed by this manifest

array_shapes.meaning: point coordinates; one point per row
full-gradient constraint or evaluation point coordinates
ordered RBF or model parameter vector
scalar constraints first, followed by full-gradient components in point-major order
one scalar prediction per value-evaluation point
scalar predictions first, followed by full-gradient predictions in point-major order
scalar-center weights, point-major gradient-center weights, then polynomial weights
lag distance for each variogram bin
pair count for each variogram bin
one estimated planarity factor per point
one generated signed-distance value per generated sample
one scalar normal-score value per input scalar
points that generated geometry should snap toward
no per-point tolerances or one relative tolerance per snap point

layout_rules.rule: Each row represents one logical point or vector.
All scalar blocks precede all full-gradient blocks.
Within a full-gradient block, all dim components for one point are contiguous before the next point.
For a Model parameter vector, nugget is first and component RBF parameters follow in model component order.

error_categories.trigger_domain: An array has the wrong rank, fixed axis width, row count, or paired-array length.
A workflow is requested outside dimensions 1, 2, and 3 or mixes incompatible dimensions.
A finite scalar, count, degree, tolerance, accuracy, radius, distance, resolution, or parameter vector violates its semantic domain.
NaN or infinity is supplied where the selected workflow does not define it as data.
Bounds are contradictory, incomplete at the logical constraint level, or incompatible with the selected operation.
A stateful result is read or used before the prerequisite calculation, fit, transform, or generation.
The selected kernel, derivative mode, dimension, model combination, or field configuration does not support the workflow.
There are too few independent observations or constraints for the requested model and polynomial space.
A warm-start or incremental state is incompatible with the model, dimension, or constraint layout.
A numerical workflow terminates without satisfying its accepted convergence condition.
A numerical workflow reaches its configured iteration limit.
Input geometry is empty, singular, locally insufficient, or otherwise cannot define the requested geometric result.
A requested artifact or geometry file cannot be read or written.
A migration-only Model or Interpolant artifact is truncated, corrupt, incompatible, or unsupported.

inputs.name: polynomial_degree
inputs.semantic_default: minimum degree required by the selected component set

input_relationships: All four point-aligned inputs have row count n.
Each point carries an accepted equality, lower-bound, upper-bound, or combined logical constraint.
The target representation for absent logical constraints is intentionally not fixed by this manifest.
points and normals have the same row count n
each generated SDF value corresponds to the generated SDF point at the same row

research_only_observations.reason: A current local Python build success or failure is execution evidence, not an accepted workflow, signature, shape, or behavioral contract.

A suspected discrepancy between the frozen binding declaration and an underlying SDF constructor must not select a RapidRBF call signature or distance policy without separate reproducible evidence and an acceptance decision.
Observed or suspected behavior on valid inputs is neither a compatibility requirement nor an intentional difference until a frozen reproducer is captured and adjudicated.
